textbookText: 3. Which diseases are caused by the deficiency of RBC and enormous number of WBC in blood?
Ans:- Anaemia is caused by a deficiency of RBCs, and leukaemia is caused by an abnormal increase in WBCs.
4. Where does bicuspid value lie in heart?
Ans:- The bicuspid valve (mitral valve) lies between the left atrium and left ventricle of the heart.
5. What is meant by blood pressure of a man is 130/90 mmHg?
Ans:- A blood pressure of 130/90 mmHg means the systolic pressure is 130 mmHg and the diastolic pressure is 90 mmHg.
6. What is human immune system?
Ans:- The human immune system is the body’s defense system that protects against diseases and harmful microorganisms.
7. Where are red blood cells formed and destroyed?
Ans:- Red blood cells (RBCs) are formed in the bone marrow and destroyed in the liver and spleen.
8. Which part of the human heart receives impure blood and which part receives pure blood?
Ans:- The right atrium and right ventricle receive impure (deoxygenated) blood, while the left atrium and left ventricle
receive pure (oxygenated) blood.
9. WBCs are like the soldiers of body. Why?
Ans:- WBCs are called the soldiers of the body because they protect the body by fighting and destroying disease-causing
germs.
10. Which device is used to measure blood pressure?
Ans:- The device used to measure blood pressure is called a sphygmomanometer.
11. How is high or low blood pressure detected?
Ans:- High or low blood pressure is detected by measuring the pressure of blood using a sphygmomanometer and comparing
it with the normal value (120/80 mmHg).

2. Valves are present in veins but not in arteries, why?
Ans:- Veins carry blood at low pressure and against gravity, valves prevent backflow. Arteries carry blood under high
pressure from the heart, so backflow is naturally prevented, valves are not needed.
3. The wall of artery is thicker than vein, why?
Ans:- Arteries withstand high pressure of blood pumped from the heart, so their walls are thick and elastic. Veins have lower
pressure, so their walls are thinner.

5. The wall of left ventricle is thicker than the wall of right ventricle, why?
Ans:- The left ventricle pumps blood to the entire body (systemic circulation) requiring more force, so its wall is thicker. But
the right ventricle pumps blood only to the lungs (pulmonary circulation), requiring less force.

7. Right auricle is larger than left auricle, why?
Ans:- The right auricle receives blood from the whole body (via vena cava), so it is slightly larger. The left auricle receives
blood only from the lungs, so it is smaller.
